FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday October 28, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 12:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here Action Items: Staff will provide the course withdrawal legislation to the Graduate Student Association and ask that they review and comment in advance of the 11/19 senate meeting.
Sen.
Chen will liaise with the ACC Chair regarding the College of Education proposal to ensure that the committee’s feedback is part of the senate discussion.
Staff will prepare a slide showing upcoming years in which the Wednesday before Thanksgiving might be used as a class day.
Staff will prepare a list of senators eligible to serve on both FSEC and as senate vice president and will transmit the information to the committee.
Sen.
Van Wyk will encourage the SCLC Chair to think about a work plan for the full academic year so they might address their own priorities (DEI climate) as well as those forwarded by FSEC (mid-level faculty support, and uncompensated service burdens for senior faculty).
Sen.

Meyerson volunteered to look into other faculty senates at comparable institutions to see what types of actions or responses have been forthcoming in light of the incident at Cornell and similar situations. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Preisser called the meeting to order at 10:00 am.
VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, Meyerson, and Chen were present.
Past President Travis Williams was also on hand. 2.
Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 10/21/26 FSEC meeting.
The minutes were approved as edited. 3.
Priority Items and New Business 3.1.
Advance Planning for the November 19 FS meeting - 3.1.1 Status of Legislation: ● Course withdrawals legislation and back-up - Pres.
Preisser provided revised legislation and the associated slide deck for the meeting.
At the request of the graduate school dean, the current draft excludes graduate students from the extended withdrawal period.
It was noted that peer institutions do not have separate withdrawal calendars for undergraduate versus graduate students.
Some FSEC members strongly prefer that the new deadlines apply to all students.

It was noted that, with the popularity of the '4+1'/ABM programs and other enrollment trends, both undergraduate and graduate students could be enrolled in the same course but operate under different guidelines.
FSEC was not provided with details of the graduate school dean’s rationale so any related questions from the floor would need to be fielded by her or her representative.
The student senate has provided a resolution in support of the bill and the graduate student association will be asked to review and comment as well.
Alternative language wherein graduate students are included in the expanded deadlines will be available. ● UM amendments related to University College/Fannon Institute transition - The bill has been transmitted to CBUM for a recommendation in advance of the 11/19 senate meeting. 1

● Consideration of Posthumous Degree conferral changes (UM Chp 8) EP update - Pres.
Preisser transmitted a revised version to the Provost’s office based on last week’s FSEC discussion but has not received a reply.
The bill is still expected to move forward in November. ● College of Education concern related to using the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as a class day when needed–The calendar committee has reviewed the proposal and has not arrived at consensus on a recommendation.
Liaison Chen will ask the committee chair to synthesize feedback for the senate.
Information on the years when URI would need to use either C/IP Day or the Wednesday before Thanksgiving will need to be made available as the senate deliberates. 3.1.2 College Liaisons - Incorporating feedback/next steps - FSEC agreed to try to launch a ‘trial balloon’ liaison committee this year on an all-volunteer basis, with the hope of formalizing a fully comprised special committee in the fall of 2027. 3.1.3 Service Compensation Model Forum - Pres.
Preisser presented data and slides on the senate’s ever-increasing workload and the year-round service commitment of FSEC members and especially the officers.

It was agreed that a compensation model for officers akin to small department chairs is reasonable and should be part of a formal request.
It was also agreed that non-officer FSEC members and the chairs of larger committees should receive meaningful stipends (available as pay and not faculty development funds).
Pres.
Preisser plans to present his data to the administration in advance of submitting a formal senate budget request in hopes that some agreement can be reached to modernize the compensation protocols.
If an agreement is not reached, a full presentation to the senate will be made at the November meeting, to make clear that the senate service recompense structure has not kept pace with other components of faculty pay, nor with the inflation rate, and the amount of work involved continues to increase, thereby widening the gap between workload and remuneration. 3.2.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - The Tracker has been updated to show completed items and new items will be added as they emerge. 3.3.
Committee Assignment Updates - None. 3.4.

Guidance for the newly formed Nominating Committee - Staff will prepare a list of senators eligible to serve on both FSEC and as senate vice president and will transmit the information to the committee. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Two new concerns had been submitted.
One pertained to the inability to provide an executive summary or equivalent statement in the Interfolio P&T package.
Pres.
Preisser will make a request that this be provided for as an option and report back.
The other concern related to summer demand for certain online general education courses having increased to the point that it is now impacting fall in-person enrollment in these courses.
Sections 4.60.14 and 15 of the University Manual were called out for reference, as they make clear these are department-level decisions to be made by department chairs with faculty and enrollment management input.
Pres.
Preisser will reach out to the complainant to encourage interaction with the department chair on the issue. 2

4.2.
Ongoing Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee (current draft); future forum.
VP Trimm reported that he is still awaiting feedback on his proposal from the advisory committees but is still on track for a December forum.
Sen.
Meyerson, as CBUM liaison, will follow up to make sure the committee has what it needs for review. 4.3.
Discussion: The uncompensated service burden of senior faculty - Sen.
Meyerson had raised the issue in a prior meeting and noted anecdotal evidence points sharply to a trend of burdening senior faculty with the most thankless jobs as an accommodation to junior faculty who are advised to focus on their research and gain tenure.
FSEC agreed that having some data to work with would be useful, but at its core, this seems to be a cultural issue.
FSEC also agreed that this is exactly the type of issue that should be assigned to the SCLC.
That Committee has already been approached about looking into the ‘mid-level faculty’ issue raised by Sen.
Chen over the summer and it would seem that the two problems dovetail in many ways.
Sen.

Van Wyk, as liaison to SCLC, will communicate with the Chair about developing a specific project that might address both issues, but noted that for now, the Committee Chair seems more focused on developing a survey on the DEI climate.
Sen.
Van Wyk will encourage the Committee Chair to think about a work plan for the full year.
Proper planning may permit the committee to tackle their own priorities along with those forwarded by FSEC. 4.4.
Discussion: Continued from last meeting - actions the senate might take in light of recent events at Cornell - Sen.
Meyerson volunteered to look into other faculty senates at comparable institutions to see what types of actions or responses have been forthcoming.
She will report her findings and then FSEC can decide how to proceed.
It was agreed that the substance of any remarks, resolutions, etc. should not be a reaction to the Cornell case so much as a statement on the problem of sexual violence in campuses generally.
Sen.
Van Wyk noted the PSAC has discussed the issue to some degree and noted the fact that many reported cases at URI actually occur off-campus, which raises jurisdictional questions and complicates the university’s response. 5.

Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates - Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others 5.1.1 Other Updates - Budget; College level governance concerns, etc. - Pres.
Preisser and VP Trimm have a scheduled meeting with the University President, Provost and Vice President on 11/13 and the primary topic will be the senate budget.
A recent meeting of the Stewardship Council prompted Pres.
Preisser to raise questions about the proposed Medical School and whether or not the timeline for launch is realistic.
There do not seem to be clear answers regarding the process for putting a curriculum in place (program(s), degree(s), and courses) and getting it accredited in rapid fashion.
Completing these tasks before the state’s initial funding runs out will be challenging, and will be made even more complicated by the fact that there are not personnel in place to advance the Med School curriculum.
Pres.
Preisser will continue to monitor the situation. 6.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
None. 7.
Adjournment - T he meeting adjourned at 11:51 am. 3

What does it mean to be a Faculty Senator?
URI Faculty Senate Frequently Asked Questions
What are the most important aspects of being a Senator?
1.Engaged Attendance:Presence at the monthly Senate meetings is essential,asa
quorum is needed to conduct our business.You are the voice of your colleagues,and
for equitable engagement,and helps build community,it is also possible to attend
remotely.Agendas and any supporting materials are distributed in advance of each
meeting,along with details on how to connect online.Attendance at any special events
is equally important(for example,a Senate-sponsored forum for the general faculty on
a specified topic)
standing or special committees.Depending on their individual skills or interests,some
Senators maybe asked to s it on a university joint committee in addition to or in lieu of
a standing committee assignment.Senate work often begins with careful consideration
by one or more of these committees,which provide reports to the Senateand
recommend specific actions for consideration by the Senate as a whole.Committee

chairs work with committee members and the Senate staff to hold regular meetings
online or in person throughout the year.Committee business ebbs and flows and
workloads vary.Your committee may have pressing work to do one semester,andless
work the next This is not unexpected or unusual
3.Communication and Input:One of the essential functions of the Senate is to facilitate
communication among faculty and between them and the administration.Thismeans
that Senators seek input of colleagues in their home department(s)and likewise report
Senate business back to your department.
Please speak to your chair about including Senate business as a regular feature of
department meetings,if this is not already the practice in your department.Withsome
rare exceptions,the issues discussed in the meetings of the full Senate area matter of
public record.

Who may attend Faculty Senate meetings and where are they held?
Any member of the URl community or the general public may attend a Faculty Senate
meeting.However,only voting members of the Senate may vote on legislation,resolutions,
officer elections,and any other business raised at the meeting.Bylaws stipulate that only
Senators and ex officio members have the RIGHT to speak during meetings.Exofficio
members participate in discussions,ask questions,and make and second motions;theyare
not,however,allowed tovote.Non-senators may request to speak at a meeting beforehand
via the online Permission To Speak”form found on the Faculty Senate website.To facilitate
the meeting itself
Meetings take place throughout the academic year in the Hope Roomof the Higgins
Welcome Center from3-5p.m.monthly on a Thursday.A brief reception with refreshments is
provided at every meeting.This is a wonderful opportunity for in-person attendees to network
colleges
How are agenda items determined?
The meeting agenda is set by the Faculty Senate Executive Committee.Agenda items may
can also be suggested to the Executive Committee via an anonymous form on the Faculty

can also be suggested by a committee or introduced at a Senate meeting during the New
Business'portion.
While agenda items maybe suggested at anytime,inclusion of an item at the monthly
meeting requires the Executive Committee approve adding it to the agenda atleast one week
in advance of the scheduled senate meeting.This is necessary for timely agenda posting and
motion in realtime are typically considered for inclusion on a future agenda or referred to a
standing or special committee for further exploration.Exceptions to this timeline are reserved
for unusually urgent or time-sensitive Issues.
Doesthe Faculty Senate use parliamentary procedures to conduct meetings?
The Senate relies upon the American Institute of Parliamentarians Standard Codeof
Parliamentary Procedure.Guidebooks and other reference materials are available in the
Faculty Senate Office.Training on procedural basics is provided during the annual
Orientation meeting.This meeting is held each September and is required for all new
Senators(and highly recommended as a refresher for ALL Senators).

wait to be recognized by the President tospeak.Senators may not interject or interrupt a
their comments and accurate minutes can be produced.
